title: Agentic LLMs for Social Network Generation using Explainable Adversarial Re-prompting

problem.claim: Real-world social networks are difficult to use directly because of privacy regulations and ethical concerns, creating a need for social network generation techniques.

gap.claim: Existing LLM-based social network simulation lacks comprehensive guidance for generating sufficiently realistic social networks.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes X-ARP, a social network generation method integrating agentic LLMs with explainable adversarial re-prompting.
The framework uses graph-prompted environment perception and decision-making to simulate autonomous agent behaviors for constructing social networks.
The framework incorporates an explainable bot detector that extracts multi-dimensional realism evidence and feeds it back as re-prompts to refine the generator.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that X-ARP significantly outperforms existing methods, with a 2.22% deviation in macro-structural metrics and a 10.5% improvement in semantic realism.

narrative_sequence.summary: High-quality social network data are important for social computing research.
Privacy and ethical constraints motivate synthetic social network generation.
LLM-based simulation lacks comprehensive guidance for producing realistic networks.
X-ARP combines agentic LLM generation with explainable detection, feedback, and iterative adversarial refinement.
The authors report improved structural and semantic realism relative to existing methods.

source_observation.claim: Explainable detector outputs are converted into re-prompts that guide the generator toward behaviors closer to real-world activities.

interpretation.claim: Interpretable evaluation feedback can be used as an iterative control signal for improving generated artifacts.

application.claim: For other generative simulation tasks, connect generation with an explainable evaluator and feed localized evidence back into subsequent generation steps.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this feedback strategy generalizes beyond social network generation.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, experimental protocol, or statistical uncertainty.
The abstract does not describe the bot detector architecture or the multi-level explanation mechanism in implementation detail.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility of the reported results.
